name: set_coin_ratios
doc:
Write every coin's ratio in ONE state publish.

Exists for editors that collect a whole allocation before committing it — a
sheet that cannot stream state back per keystroke, so it hands over the
finished split. Looping one-coin batches is not equivalent: each call
publishes, so the basket would be seen at intermediate totals, and a later
call being refused would leave the earlier ones applied.

**All-or-nothing.** The batch is rejected outright if any ratio is out of
`0..=100`, any coin is not in the basket, or any coin appears twice. Applying
the acceptable subset would leave a total that is not 100, which the user
cannot correct without re-editing — refusing keeps the last good allocation.

FSM for the multi-order submit. `Idle` before any submit; `Loading`
after the action's sync flip; `Success` / `Error` on completion.
Enum-typed, so it carries **no** `#[uniffi(default)]` — a bare
`#[uniffi(default)]` on an enum field compiles under cargo and then
breaks bindgen for both Swift and Kotlin.

fields.name: submit_error
fields.doc:
Raw underlying error text from the submit — `None` while idle /
loading / on success. Native owns the surrounding localized copy and
dispatches on the error code it already received via the vended
place-order error handler; Rust holds only the raw text.

fields.name: submit_error_code
fields.doc:
Positive business code (`sCode`) of a rejected submit, as a string —
`None` on success, while idle/loading, and for transport-level failures.
Same shape as `interactors/dca/contract_dca/edit_params.rs:216`.

Native's vended place-order error handler DISPATCHES ON THIS
(`OKTPOErrorHandler.m:56-111`): five branches key off `error.code`, and the
generic arm resolves its copy through `[OKTPODataFactory poErrorInfo:error.code]`
before falling back to the message. Reporting the failure as `submit_error`
alone dropped the one field that decides what the user sees, which is half of
why a rejection could produce no affordance at all (QA #14).

fields.name: left_lever
fields.doc:

Added for Wave C1's final batch: when `OKTSArbLegContentHost` takes over
`OKTPOContextDataDelegate`, it must source every context value from Rust
instead of reading it back off native's child VCs. Every other member
already had a state field; `lever` was the one gap
(`OKTASPOContentVC.m:912` reads `buttonLineVC.leverValue` into
`params.lever` on the pre-check sheet).

Not on the submit wire — the multi-order body carries no `lever`
(`getCommitArbitrageParams` never sets it). Pre-check display only, so an
empty value must stay empty rather than defaulting to `"1"`, which would
assert a leverage the user never chose.

fields.name: left_direction
fields.doc:

This is the SINGLE source for the leg's direction: [`Self::left_side`] and
[`Self::left_pos_side`] are derived from it by
[`ArbitragePlaceOrderActions::set_left_direction`], so side and posSide can
never disagree with the identity the user picked. Before Wave C1 the native
direction VC owned the identity and pushed side/posSide separately, which
is exactly the shape that let them drift.

Empty until the direction control seeds it. Empty is NOT coerced to a
default direction — an unset direction must read as unset, or the confirm
sheet would show a direction the user never chose.

fields.name: spread_rate_display
fields.doc:
Display twin of [`Self::spread_rate_value`].

The raw field is the unscaled ratio `(left - right) / right`; native shows
a SIGNED PERCENT. Before this twin existed the iOS Rust arm passed the raw
ratio straight into the shared price-settings label, so a spread native
rendered as `+0.31%` appeared as `0.0030749…`.

Native leaf (`OKTArbStgyUtil.getDepthSpreadRateText`, m:31-42):
`[[gap okt_divide:right].treatAsPercentage.prependPlusSign
toLocalizedStringDownToMax:2]`, with `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` ("--")
when either input string is empty.

Three-way, matching native's three outcomes exactly:
- `None` — the two legs' quote currencies differ. Native calls
`updateSpreadRateWith:@""` (no text at all), NOT the "--" placeholder.
- `Some(Placeholder)` — units match but an input is absent/unparseable →
native's `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder`.
- `Some(Percent{..})` — the real value.

Enum-typed → **no `#[uniffi(default)]`** (a bare one compiles under cargo
then breaks bindgen on both platforms).

`None` is load-bearing: it is the pre-first-fetch state, in which native has

default-filled row would instead render five zeros, which reads as real data.

"fetched, no rows", so native cannot tell them apart either and the lever
control renders the same placeholder for both.

`ccy` param convention.

quote ccy for LastPrice (:1719). `getMarginUnit` and `getPnlUnit` are
literal aliases of one another (`BotConverter.kt:120-121`) that return

legs: its split-colour binder path never calls
`nextLineTextView.setTextOrGone` (`BotListFieldDataBinder.kt:235-254`),

click on `subItemType` (:176-180) — keying off `tooltip` alone, as spot
does, would leave GridProfit's label tap dead.

doc:
One Contract Grid Overview field-grid row.

Shape follows [`SpotGridOverviewRowPresentation`] with TWO additions,
because contract rows carry two INDEPENDENT affordances that spot's single
channel cannot express: GridProfit has a label sheet AND a withdraw icon
(:1513 + :1514), and ExtraMargin has a label tooltip AND an edit icon
(:1698 + :1699).

[`intent`](Self::intent) deliberately keeps SPOT'S meaning — the ICON
channel — because spot's shipped binder wires `row.intent` to
`ivDrawableType` and `contentDrawableClick` while routing `row.tooltip` to
`subItemClick`. The new channel is therefore named
[`label_intent`](Self::label_intent) rather than redefining `intent`, so the
identically-named field cannot mean opposite things on the two records.

doc:
One selectable scheduled-check period offered by `GET /priapi/v5/algo/public/config`'s `intervalOptions`
list (ALGO-43412 combined mode). Only bot types supporting combined rebalance return the field.

`key` is the period in MINUTES and is what gets submitted as the bot's `interval`; both natives map it straight
into their own option models (Android `IntervalOption(key: Int)`, iOS `options.map { $0.key }`), which is why it is
`i32` and not `u32` — `u32` would generate `kotlin.UInt` and force casts on the Android side, and `i64` would
generate `kotlin.Long`. `value` is the label ALREADY localised by the server and is rendered verbatim: natives
have no client-side formatter, so rows with a blank `value` are filtered out during projection and every option
reaching native is displayable. The list is honestly empty when the server omits the field — no fallback is
seeded here.

`Eq` is the one addition to the neighbouring records' derive set: `SmartPortfolioPublicConfig` holds a
`Vec<IntervalOptionInfo>` and already derives `Eq`, which a `PartialEq`-only element type would break.

**Gap R-F5 (Wave R3).** Modelled solely so the Rust arm can satisfy

`feeList.first?.feeCcy` (`OKTInstrumentDisplayUtil.swift:923`). The Invest-More
and Edit-Amount sheet factories take a `model:` argument typed as that
protocol composition, so without this field the Rust arm has no way to supply
a conforming object built from typed data — forcing the legacy

but nothing on the detail path reads it, and `public_types.md`'s

holds.

anything else → "Trade with" (native `OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:306-312`).
Appended field — `#[uniffi(default = "")]` keeps the pre-existing Swift
construction site (`SmartIcebergDetailNativeProvider.swift:319`) source

fields.name: start_trigger
fields.doc:
Start-trigger condition, selected out of the wire `triggerParams`
array by `triggerAction == "start"` — the Rust port of native
`OKTStgyInfoModel.startTriggerModel` (`OKTStgyInfoModel.m:131-136`).

entirely). Native's getter returns nil there, every `isIndicator*`
message to nil answers `NO`, and the Info tab's Start Condition row
falls through to `--` with no tap affordance — identical rendering to
`Some(_)` with `indicator == Unsupported`. Both states are preserved
rather than flattened so a "server sent nothing" bug stays
distinguishable from "server sent a literal we don't render".

Appended field — `#[uniffi(default = None)]` keeps the pre-existing
Swift construction site (`SmartIcebergDetailNativeProvider.swift:319`)
source-compatible across the bindings regen, per ffi-evolution rule 3.
The literal is spelled out because a bare `#[uniffi(default)]` breaks
bindgen on both platforms.

family's `price_dig` → **FLOOR**.

fields.name: average_price_display
fields.doc:
A11 — the allocation cell's average price. `price_dig`, **FLOOR**.

⚠️ Deliberately DIFFERENT from [`Self::average_price_round_display`],
which formats the **same** `avg_px` with HALF_UP for the multi-coin
aggregate line. Native genuinely uses two rounding directions for one
wire value (cell: `toLocalizedStringDown`; aggregate:
`chargeConvertor.toQuoteFormated(avgPx).round`). Asserted as a divergence
in the tests — do not "unify" them.

fields.name: average_price_round_display
fields.doc:

**HALF_UP** at `price_dig`. See the warning on
[`Self::average_price_display`].

fields.name: cumulated_buy_display
fields.doc:
A12 — cumulated buy quantity. Native `toLocalizedStringDown(toMax:)` at
the family's index-config `base_dig` → **FLOOR**. Note this is the BASE
digit, not the price digit its neighbouring rows use.

fields.name: pnl_display

A15 — per-coin PnL. Native
`OKTStgyPnlDispalyUtil.localizedPnl(withPnl:precision:)` at the bot's
profit precision; the `.appendCurrency(quoteUnit)` suffix stays on the
Swift row (the unit lives on the parent as `quote_unit`).

Colour travels **inside** the twin (`BotPnlColor`), replacing native's
separate `OKTStgyPnlDispalyUtil.pnlColor(withPnl:precision:)` call — one
derivation instead of two, so text and colour cannot disagree.

`treatAsPercentage` → `toLocalizedStringRoundToMax:2` (HALF-UP, max 2,
trailing zeros dropped).

field: the allocation **cell** renders it *uncapped*
(`.treatAsPercentage().toLocalizedString()`,
`RecurringBuyCryptoAllocationCellInfoViewState.swift:147-148`) while the
aggregate line rounds to 2 (`OKTSOrderListUtil.m`,
`OKTSRecurringDisplayTypeRatio`). Collapsing them into one value rendered
`"33.333%"` on the aggregate line where native shows `"33.33%"`.

Same deliberate-divergence shape as
[`Self::average_price_display`] (FLOOR, cell) vs
[`Self::average_price_round_display`] (HALF_UP, aggregate) — do not merge
either pair.

fields.name: cell_ratio_display

`treatAsPercentage().toLocalizedString()`.

The cell half of the R-B20 pair. [`Self::aggregate_ratio_display`] is the
aggregate half and rounds HALF-UP at 2. Do not merge them.

## Why a counter is needed at all

`stop_state` / `stop_error` are STICKY: they settle at
`Success`/`Error` and stay there until the next invocation. A foreign
consumer therefore cannot distinguish "the terminal I am already showing"
from "a new terminal that happens to look identical", because a
UniFFI Record state cannot be mutated from the foreign side — there is
nothing for the consumer to clear.

Consumers work around that by latching on the value, which silently
swallows two consecutive IDENTICAL failures — exactly the case a user hits
by retrying a failing action. Pairing the terminal with this id makes each
invocation distinguishable: latch on `(attempt, state)`, not on `state`.

## Bumped on EVERY invocation, including the rejected ones

The pre-validation branch in each action is itself a terminal and reaches
`Error` with no `Loading` in between, so a repeated rejection would
otherwise produce no state change whatsoever. The bump lives inside the
same `modify_state` as each branch's own writes, so it costs no extra
observer notification.

Wraps rather than saturates: identity only needs to CHANGE, and a
saturated counter would stop changing.

Additive — `#[uniffi(default = 0)]` keeps every existing foreign
construction site compiling.

name: SmartArbitrageActionDescriptor
doc:
One Rust-owned More-sheet action. `label` is a semantic `SmartArbitrageActionLabel`,
resolved by native the same way `icon` already is — an exhaustive mapping to a
concrete resource, not a string lookup that can fail at runtime.

No `disabled_reason` / `disabled_message`: legacy has no disable path for any item
this catalog currently emits. Both can be added later as `Option<...>` fields with
`#[uniffi(default = None)]` without breaking the generated Swift/Kotlin constructors.

name: release

Stop-gap teardown (TEMPORARY — target state is the stream APIs,

One idempotent call at host lifecycle end that breaks the
UniFFI handleMap cycle for any registered callback observers,
ends active streams, and stops effects. On Kotlin call BEFORE
`destroy()`. Includes `stop()`.
